title: Tanzanian Cassava Pudding
community: Coastal Tanzania — the cassava dessert tradition
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Pudini ya Muhogo — fresh grated cassava baked with coconut milk, sugar, and cardamom into a dense, chewy, golden-crusted pudding. The coastal Tanzanian baked cassava dessert — a naturally gluten-free, completely local preparation with a uniquely satisfying texture.
longDesc: Cassava pudding is one of the most traditional Tanzanian coastal desserts — grated cassava, coconut milk, sugar, and cardamom, baked until the top caramelises and the interior becomes dense and slightly chewy. It is the dessert of the coast's most practical kitchens, using the most available ingredients to produce something genuinely special.
ingredients: 500g fresh cassava — peeled and finely grated
// Optional: ½ cup desiccated coconut folded in
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease baking dish.
Squeeze excess moisture from grated cassava through a clean cloth.
Combine cassava, coconut milk, sugar, cardamom, vanilla, eggs, and salt. Mix thoroughly.
Bake 35—40 minutes until the top is golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
chefTips: Squeezing moisture from the cassava is essential — wet cassava produces a soggy pudding.
The top should be deep golden — this is where the most flavour is.
Cool before cutting — it firms as it cools.
cookingScience: Cassava starch gelatinises during baking — the starch granules absorb the coconut milk and egg proteins, forming a dense gel matrix. The top layer caramelises through Maillard reactions and caramelisation of the natural sugars, creating the characteristic golden, slightly crispy crust over the soft interior.
sustainabilityTips: Fresh cassava — Tanzania's most climate-resilient crop.
culturalNote: Cassava pudding is coastal Tanzania's most grounded dessert — made from what grows everywhere, with the coconut that is always available, producing something completely satisfying without needing anything imported. It is the dessert of self-sufficiency and abundance.
